questions.qtext: Based on the ER diagram shown above, which of the following options is/are True?

options.text: Each course has at least one student.
Every student has taken at least one course.

questions.solution:
Answer: A, D

Source solution 1 (score: 0)

A is true: The double lines on the course side signify Total Participation, meaning every course in the database must connect to at least one student.

B is false: The single line on the student side signifies Partial Participation, meaning a student can exist without being registered in any course.

C is false: The directed arrowhead pointing toward course indicates a Many-to-One mapping from student to course, restricting each student to a maximum of 1 course.

D is true: The many-to-one constraint allows multiple distinct students to map to the same individual course simultaneously, so a course can easily have 3 students.

so A and D are true

questions.qtext:
The figure with ovals and circles below illustrates a relationship set between two entity sets. Each circle is an entity or relationship, and the edges connect them. The ER diagram right below that figure needs to be complete with constraints that are consistent with the edges in the diagram. For each of the following, match the statements with the correct constraint:

\[
\begin{array}{l@{\hspace{4cm}}l}
\textbf{Statements:} & \textbf{Constraints:} \\[2mm]
\text{a) A bold edge between E1 and R is:} &
\text{i) needed} \\[1mm]
\text{b) An arrowhead between E1 and R is:} &
\text{ii) optional} \\[1mm]
\text{c) A bold edge between E2 and R is:} &
\text{iii) disallowed} \\[1mm]
\text{d) An arrowhead between E2 and R is:} &
\end{array}
\]


$\textbf{Choose the correct combination:}$
questions.solution:
Answer: A

Source solution 1 (score: 0)
In mapping diagram We can see that Minimum is 0 from E1 to R that is E1 can exists without E2 so there must not be any bold edge between E1 and R option B and D are eliminated
We can also see that 3rd and 4th instance of E1 is mapping to to single So there cant be arrowhead too therefore option A is correct
